cues.text: An Irish nobleman who traded a life of comfort for the wandering life of a monk, Columbanus set out from Bangor Abbey with twelve companions determined to bring Irish monastic rigor to a continental Church he judged badly in need of reform.

He founded Luxeuil in the forests of Gaul and, when his blunt criticism of the Frankish court's morals finally cost him that monastery, pressed on through Switzerland into northern Italy rather than turn back.
There, in his final years, he founded Bobbio, which would grow into one of medieval Europe's great centers of learning and manuscript preservation.

He was never formally canonized in a Church that had not yet developed the process, yet Rome has kept his feast for over a thousand years, and Pope Benedict XVI would later call him, simply, 'a European saint.'
